surfaces.part: light green grass ground fading into dark green grass edge (flat terrain tile)

answer.evidence: The tile is a full 16x16 opaque square. Its left side (x=4) is uniform light green (#759951) for rows 0-15, and its right side (x=11) is mostly dark green (#375a27) with a few lighter speckles. This is a flat ground autotile with a horizontal transition from light to dark grass. It has no front face, no eave line, no ellipse and no vertical face, so it reads as a flat top-down terrain tile, which is expected for terrain.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a grass-type ground patch, so it matches the reference kind. It is drawn small on the board, so my judgement of structure is limited and rests partly on the measured facts. It shows a light-to-dark green ramp with scattered speckle dots and a darker edge band, and no outline. The measured facts are 8 visible tones per tile against 3 for the reference grass and 7 for the paving, 0% near-flat coverage, and 0% neutral dark edge pixels, so the dark tones are tinted green rather than black. Total distinct colours are only 8 against 80 for the reference grass, but the palette is locked and the visible tones are not lower. No 5x5 area is a flat fill. Texture is somewhat more regular than the reference's irregular tufts, so I rate it 'some' rather than 'rich'. It is not shallower than the reference grass.
